subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: The rule delegates wholly to §11.9.11, so I read §11.9.11.2 (spec lines 11970-11990) rather than stopping at the pointer: rule 2 is the standard-binary block -- a) NEAREST-EVEN implied when the INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause is absent; b) NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO SHALL NOT be specified; c) NEAREST-EVEN rounds to the nearest exactly-representable SBIDI value whose rightmost bit is zero; d) PROHIBITED + inexact => EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION and undefined results; e) TRUNCATION rounds toward zero. READ: OptionsBinder.cs:60-61 maps the clause through RoundingModes.MapIntermediate into OptionsModel.IntermediateRounding; OptionsModel.cs:41-44 gives that property the unconditional default `CobolRounding.NearestAwayFromZero`, its doc comment citing '§11.9.11 r3' -- the standard-DECIMAL rule 3a default. There is NO arm on ArithmeticMode anywhere in the default: rule 2a's NEAREST-EVEN implication is absent, and rule 2b's prohibition on NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO under standard-binary is never checked (grep of src/ for IntermediateRounding returns exactly the six sites above plus NumericRenderer.IntermediateMode at NumericRenderer.cs:396, which stringifies the mode into the CobolDec calls and is reached only from the StandardDecimal routing). Rules 2c/2d/2e cannot exist without an SBIDI, which does not exist (see GR-8.8.1.4.2-1). Compounding it, DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects the mode outright (COBOL0806), so none of this is reachable. Editions 2014,2023 (same derivation). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a standard-binary arm on the IntermediateRounding default (NEAREST-EVEN), a COBOL#### diagnostic for rule 2b, SBIDI-level implementations of 2c/2d/2e, and goldens per leg. Deliberately NOT cited: StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported (pins the rejection, not the rounding). || UPHELD: I read §11.9.11.2 myself at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:11970-12000 -- rule 2's five sub-items are exactly as the adjudicator renders them (2a NEAREST-EVEN implied, 2b NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO shall not be specified, 2c rightmost-bit-zero, 2d PROHIBITED => EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION + undefined, 2e TRUNCATION toward zero), and rule 3a is the standard-DECIMAL NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO default. READ OptionsModel.cs:41-44: `public CobolRounding IntermediateRounding { get; init; } = CobolRounding.NearestAwayFromZero;` with the doc comment 'Default ... when absent (§11.9.11 r3)' -- unconditional, no ArithmeticMode arm, exactly as claimed; and OptionsBinder.cs:61 `if (c.intermediateRoundingClause()?.intermediateRoundingMode() is { } ir) return m with { IntermediateRounding = RoundingModes.MapIntermediate(ir) };` has no mode-awareness either, so rule 2b's prohibition genuinely has no enforcement site. NEW FINDING (minor, citation hygiene -- CLAUDE.md rule 1's exact failure mode): that doc comment's '§11.9.11 r3' is written ONE LEVEL SHORT -- §11.9.11 has no numbered rules; the rule is §11.9.11.2 rule 3 a). The same short form appears on OptionsModel.DefaultRounding ('§11.9.6 r2', where the rules live in §11.9.6.3) and on OptionsModel.Arithmetic ('§11.9.5.2 r4', which IS correct). Cosmetic today, but it is the citation shape the project has twice let propagate into goldens. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
